patch.title: 2AR-FE Engine Oil Level Drops Between Services — Owner Reports
patch.description: Owner discussions document oil consumption on individual RAV4 vehicles with the 2AR-FE engine. Oil-pressure warning or engine noise if the level becomes dangerously low

patch.title: 2AZ-FE Brief Rattle During Cold Start — Owner Reports
patch.description: RAV4 owner discussions document a brief rattle during cold startup on individual 2AZ-FE vehicles. A sound alone does not prove VVT-i camshaft-gear, chain, tensioner, oil-pressure, accessory or valvetrain failure, and the reports do not establish a mileage band or damage progression. Toyota T-SB-0041-13 Rev1 is a VIN-gated 2AR-FE Camry bulletin, not evidence for this 2AZ-FE RAV4 topic.
patch.solution: Record the first start after an overnight soak and note duration, oil level, oil grade, warning lights and any persistent noise. Check oil pressure and condition, stored codes, accessory drive and valve-timing data using the exact 2AZ-FE procedure before disassembly. Persistent or worsening rattle, an oil-pressure warning or abnormal running needs prompt diagnosis.
symptoms: Brief rattle immediately after a cold start
Noise duration or intensity changes over time
Persistent rattle or warning light requiring prompt diagnosis

patch.description: Owner complaint listings include individual 2019 RAV4 braking events attributed by drivers to the Pre-Collision System. patch.solution: Preserve time, speed, road, weather, nearby objects, warning sequence, dash-camera evidence and PCS settings. Maintain control and arrange Toyota diagnosis of stored PCS, brake and chassis data. Inspect sensor visibility and alignment after windshield, grille, collision or suspension work. Report a safety event to NHTSA. Do not promise an update or disable a safety system as a permanent repair from this page.

PCS warning associated with an event
Driver reports no apparent obstacle for the intervention

patch.title: 2019 RAV4 Front-Seat Discomfort on Longer Drives — Owner Reports
patch.description: RAV4 owner discussions document lower-back, hip or leg discomfort on longer drives. Comfort is subjective and varies with body dimensions, seating posture, trip duration, trim, manual versus power seat, cushion-angle and lumbar equipment. The reports do not establish a model-wide seat defect, onset time, height-defined population or trade-in frequency.
patch.solution: Use the exact owner's-guide adjustments for seat distance, back angle, driver height, cushion-front angle and lumbar support where equipped, while preserving safe pedal reach and airbag posture. Take breaks on long trips and seek medical guidance for persistent pain. Do not install seat-jacker hardware, cushions or wiring-affecting modifications from this page; changes can affect restraint geometry and occupancy sensors.
symptoms: Lower-back, hip or leg discomfort during longer drives
Pressure or posture concern that changes with seat adjustment

patch.description: A law-firm investigation page and owner discussion document allegations of RAV4 windshield cracking. They are not a court finding, Toyota campaign, NHTSA investigation or defect determination and do not prove no-impact causation, thin glass, frequency or blanket warranty treatment. The crack origin, edge, glass, aperture, molding, prior work and external damage require inspection.
patch.solution: Avoid driving when a crack obstructs vision or compromises safe operation. Photograph the crack before repair and have the origin and surrounding glass inspected for impact and edge evidence. Replace glass by exact VIN and equipment. Toyota states that the forward camera must be recalibrated after windshield replacement; confirm driver-assistance operation before returning the vehicle to service.

Crack spreading from an edge or an uncertain origin
Crack enters the driver's field of view

patch.title: 2019 RAV4 Road or Tire Noise — Owner Report
patch.description: An owner discussion documents wind and tire or road noise in an individual RAV4. It does not establish a twelve-year cabin-insulation defect, measured threshold, common cause or affected population. Tire model, size, pressure and wear, alignment, wheel bearings, road surface, body seals, roof equipment and loose trim can materially change cabin noise.
patch.solution: Reproduce the noise on a consistent road and speed, verify tire size and cold pressure, inspect wear, balance, alignment and wheel bearings, and check body seals, roof accessories, underbody panels and loose cargo. Compare with a like-configured vehicle when possible. Do not buy tires or install sound-deadening until the source is isolated and fitment is confirmed.
symptoms: Road or tire noise that changes with pavement or speed
Wind-like noise that changes with direction or crosswind

patch.title: 2017 RAV4 Brake Pulsation, Noise, or Wear — Owner Complaints
patch.description: Owner complaint listings document brake concerns on some 2017 RAV4s. They do not establish a rotor or pad defect, premature-wear rate, cause or universal repair. Pulsation and vibration can result from rotor thickness variation, lateral or hub runout, corrosion or material transfer, caliper and pad condition, wheel or tire variation, or suspension looseness.
patch.solution: Confirm the exact symptom and whether it occurs during braking. Inspect pad thickness, caliper movement, hardware, tires, wheels, suspension and hubs, then measure rotor thickness variation and lateral runout using Toyota specifications. Correct the measured cause and verify wheel-fastener torque. Do not select pads or rotors from this page without exact fitment and measurements.
symptoms: Brake-pedal pulsation
Steering-wheel or body vibration while braking
Brake noise or wear concern requiring measurement

communityRecommendations.content: If stopping performance changes, grinding occurs, or a warning light appears, stop driving and arrange prompt brake inspection.

patch.title: 2019 RAV4 Power Liftgate Stops or Does Not Respond — Owner Report
patch.description: An owner report documents a 2019 RAV4 power-liftgate malfunction. One report does not establish a five-year defect, relay, sensor, module or strut cause, software remedy or report count. Toyota's guidance distinguishes system enablement, opening-height selection, obstruction and jam protection, kick-sensor conditions and environmental limits.
patch.solution: Confirm the vehicle is equipped with the power back door, verify the feature and opening-height settings, remove ice or external load, and note which switch input fails and whether warnings or unusual sounds occur. Do not force the door or replace parts by symptom. Have Toyota test 12-volt voltage, switches, sensors, spindles, wiring and stored body data using the exact VIN configuration.
symptoms: Power liftgate stops during travel
Liftgate does not respond to one or more inputs
Liftgate behavior changes with settings or environmental conditions
